claims.text: Eutectic high-entropy alloys commonly possess lamellar or rod-like eutectic microstructures containing soft FCC and hard BCC or intermetallic phases.
The relevant EHEAs can be fabricated by standard casting methods.
Post-solidification aging at 400–600°C can promote nano-precipitation.
Aging at 400–600°C produces nano-precipitates specifically at eutectic interfaces.
Optimizing aging duration can yield fine precipitates while avoiding their coarsening.
The aging treatment forms uniformly distributed, nanoscale precipitates at eutectic interfaces.
Nano-precipitates obstruct dislocation motion and thereby produce precipitation strengthening.
Controlling precipitate morphology and distribution can mitigate the harmful effect of reinforcing precipitates on ductility.
Fine, evenly dispersed precipitates prevent premature localization of deformation.
Fine, evenly dispersed precipitates encourage strain hardening across the dual-phase eutectic microstructure.
Appropriate precipitation can simultaneously improve strength and plasticity.
The aged EHEA will have higher yield strength than the as-cast baseline.
The aged EHEA will have higher ultimate tensile strength than the as-cast baseline.
The aged EHEA will maintain or improve tensile ductility relative to the as-cast baseline while its strength increases.
The magnitude of the mechanical-property changes depends on aging parameters and alloy composition.
The simultaneous strength–ductility benefit is restricted to an optimal aging window of approximately 400–600°C.
Excessively high aging temperatures can dissolve nanoscale precipitates and replace them with coarser precipitates.
Excessively long aging causes precipitate coarsening and loss of the simultaneous strength–ductility improvement.
TEM and EBSD can be used to quantify nanoscale precipitate size and spatial distribution at eutectic interfaces.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant simultaneous increase in strength and ductility, or observation of a strength–ductility trade-off, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome permits either an as-cast or a standard-annealed comparator, whereas the baseline field defines the comparator specifically as the as-cast alloy.
